newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond mart calm before Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond mart calm before Fed meeting.

text.p: A calm settled across the investment-grade and high-yield U.S. corporate bond markets on Monday, as investors awaited the Federal Reserve's decision on monetary policy on Tuesday, traders said.
"The market is very quiet. There is litte liquidity and high apathy," said one investment-grade bond trader. "Investors feel they can hang out and wait for the Fed to move before doing their buying."
Most market players were expecting the Fed to tighten 25 basis points on Tuesday, but few worried it would have a negative effect on high-grade or junk bonds.
"To the extent (a 25 basis point increase) resolves uncertainty, it can be a slight positive, although I think it will be limited by quarter-end pressure." said an investment-grade bond trader.
The trader noted investment-grade spreads have already widened around eight to 10 basis points partly due to nervousness over the Treasury market.

He said once companies report their quarter-end results in early April, high-grade bond prices could rebound slightly. He said earnings for the current quarter are unlikely to be affected by interest rate changes.
A high--yield trader said price levels in the junk bond market already reflected 25 basis points in Fed tightening.
"This move has already been priced in. Our market tends to lag Treasuries so it's inevitable that when the Treasury market dumped on itself, our market widened out," he said.
He added, "The junk market is so credit specific. It's hard to generalize about what the long-run impact will mean."

With many investors sharing such apathy, traders said trading volume in the corporate bond markets was particularly low on Monday. Prices among high-grades tracked Treasuries, while those of junk bonds were unchanged, they said.
Primary market activity was also stilted on Monday, consiting of only two straight-corporate bond deals and a handful of trust preferred offerings.
International Lease Financing Corp, a unit of American International Group Inc, sold $100 million in three-year debt to yield 6.657 percent via BancAmerica Securities Inc.
Late in the day, Spanish Broadcasting System Inc raised $250 million in a 144a offering of senior notes and exchangeable PIK preferred stock.
The company is a spanish language radio operator based in New York City.
Spanish Broadcasting priced $75 million senior notes to yield 11 percent and $175 million of senior exchangeable PIK preferred stock to yield a 14.25 percent dividend rate.
In order to intice investors to buy the bonds and exchangeable preferred stock, the offering also included warrants for 9.50 percent of the company.
In credit-specific news, Repap Wisconsin bonds were bid lower on news that Canadian paper manufacturer, Avenor rejected a merger proposal by pulp and paper rival, Domtar Inc.

Repap Wisconsin 9-1/4 percent notes were down 1/4 point to 100-1/4 bid. The company's 9-7/8 percent notes were also down about 1/4 to a 100-1/4 bid. Traders noted, however, there was very little trading in the notes.

By the end of the day, the proposed Avenor/Repap merger was put in doubt after officials at pension fund, Caisse de depot et placement, which holds a 10 percent equity stake in Avenor, said it dissapproved over the deal.
